analysis:
Only .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py changed: an offline CI test file for the threat-review tooling (budget ledger, preflight, scanner). It has no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, billing or inference code. The supplied threat IDs, including T-041, cover provider/native-runtime assets and do not map to CI tooling.

The head adds tests for: (1) a malformed cache entry stops the scan without spend and without leaking the cached 'PRIVATE'/'secret' values or request metadata into diagnostics (head lines 403-411); (2) Sonnet integration receives source uncertainty (413-419); (3) a final reviewer's uncertainty moves from result['errors'] to result['manual_review_reasons'] and still makes merge_policy.clean return False (502-512); (4) SOL reconciling local uncertainty before the final decision permits a clean merge (514-526); (5) a failed final integration stays incomplete and retains findings (528-540); (6) head-only excerpts get complete change coordinates (542-555). It also expects an extra SOL call in the escalation sequences ([SONNET, SONNET, OPUS, SOL, SOL], lines 492 and 506).

The security-relevant part is in head lines 514-526: it asserts that clean() returns True once SOL clears uncertainty, and that the final integration stage carries needs_deeper_review. The implementation files (threat_review/merge_policy, budget_scan, paid, state) are not in this batch, so the next pass should check that real behavior matches these assertions. Fail-closed budget, ledger and settlement behavior is unchanged. No new attack surface or weakened assertions were found in the test file itself. Test servers bind to 127.0.0.1 with synthetic tokens.
